IBM.rationale: IBM's Q1 2026 results show solid fundamental health: revenue up 9.5% YoY to $15.9B, with double-digit growth in Software (+11%) and Infrastructure (+15%), operating margin expansion of 140bps, and free cash flow of $2.2B up 13% YoY (highest Q1 in a decade). The z17 mainframe cycle is driving exceptional Infrastructure growth (+48% IBM Z), and ARR reached $24.6B up 10%. However, several headwinds temper enthusiasm: (1) QoQ metrics show significant deceleration—revenue -6.2% QoQ, EPS -44.6% QoQ from a strong Q2 2025, suggesting seasonality or normalization; (2) Consulting grew only 1% at constant currency with prior signs of signings weakness; (3) the $11.6B Confluent acquisition adds debt and dilution risk and increases leverage to $66.4B total debt; (4) Federal contract cancellations ($100M) and Middle East geopoliticalitical headwinds create near-term uncertainty. Valuation has compressed significantly—PE dropped from ~50x to ~20x, P/B from ~10.7x to ~6.7x—partly due to a one-time Q1 EPS jump to partly due to the stock price decline of ~22% over the quarter. This makes IBM cheaper vs its own recent history, though the stock sold off  7%+ post-earnings despite beating estimates, reflecting market disappointment that the guidance guidance AI disruption concerns. The selloping guidance (maintaining >5% CC growth, ~$1B FCF increase) suggests the market is pricing in the beat but not a raise.
